html:
Asmara, the capital of Eritrea, was rebuilt in the late 1930s by Italy into a modernist city of cinemas, cafés, garages and villas, which UNESCO listed as a World Heritage Site in 2017.

It had been the capital of Italian Eritrea since 1897. When Mussolini prepared the invasion of Ethiopia, tens of thousands of Italians came, and architects built in the latest styles. The Fiat Tagliero service station of 1938, shaped like an aeroplane, is the most famous building.

Because Eritrea was poor and closed for much of the time since, the city changed little. It is now the heart of independent Eritrea and the seat of Isaias Afwerki's government.
